sources.title: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament
facts: Published 24 June 2026 as the CCC statutory UK progress report.
It combines final 2024 and provisional 2025 emissions with CCC analysis and delivery indicators.
CCC indicator scores and pathway assessments are not cadastral parcel measurements.

sources.title: CCC Mitigation Monitoring Framework
facts: Published June 2025 and updated June 2026.
The framework explains how CCC tracks targets, indicators, policies and delivery progress.
Monitoring-framework scores are assessment outputs, not direct greenhouse-gas observations.

sources.title: CCC Progress reports Net Zero index
facts: The current index lists the 24 June 2026 UK progress report and 25 February 2026 Scotland progress report.
It is a publication catalogue and does not independently measure emissions.

sources.title: CCC Supplementary analysis of the Seventh Carbon Budget
facts: Published 11 March 2026.
The analysis tests modelled cost and energy-security conclusions under alternative scenarios.
Scenario and cost-benefit outputs must remain distinct from observed emissions.

sources.title: CCC Local authorities and the Seventh Carbon Budget summary report
facts: Published 8 July 2026 as supporting research commissioned by the CCC.
It describes local-authority roles across buildings, transport, electricity, waste, agriculture, land use and industry.
Local delivery roles and planning powers do not establish parcel-level emissions.

sources.title: CCC letter on CO2 non-pipeline transport in UK ETS
facts: Published 7 April 2026.
The CCC advises how emissions from road, rail and smaller ships transporting captured CO2 could be treated in UK ETS.
Recommended factors and allowance treatment are accounting policy, not exact vehicle or parcel measurements.

sources.title: CCC Progress in reducing emissions in Scotland 2025 report
facts: Published 25 February 2026.
The report assesses Scotland territorial emissions, targets, sector pathways and policy delivery.
Country-level emissions and pathway assessments do not bind values to cadastral parcels.

sources.title: CCC letter to Environmental Audit Committee on Seventh Carbon Budget
facts: Published 2 February 2026.
The letter explains the recommended 535 MtCO2e Seventh Carbon Budget for 2038 to 2042 and the modelled Balanced Pathway.
A future carbon-budget cap or modelled pathway is not an observed emission quantity.

sources.title: CCC letter on UK ETS and international maritime emissions
facts: Published 13 February 2026.
The CCC supports inclusion of international maritime emissions in UK ETS without increasing the overall allowance cap.
Scheme coverage and cap advice are not physical emissions measurements.

sources.title: CCC letter on draft Airports National Policy Statement
facts: Published 4 June 2026.
The letter concerns future CCC advice on aviation and cross-economy carbon budgets in the context of airport policy.
A policy letter and future advice timetable are not observed aviation emissions.

sources.title: CCC onshore petroleum advice letter
facts: Published 21 January 2026.
The letter discusses England onshore petroleum production and production emissions in the context of carbon budgets.
Production shares and pathway projections do not establish parcel-level measured emissions.

sources.title: GOV.UK Carbon Budgets guidance
facts: Updated 13 July 2026 with the Seventh Carbon Budget.
The Seventh Carbon Budget is 535 MtCO2e for 2038 to 2042 and includes the UK share of international aviation and shipping.
A five-year legal cap is not an annual or parcel emissions observation.

sources.title: Carbon budget and growth delivery plan
facts: Published 29 October 2025 and updated 23 June 2026.
The plan sets out policies and proposals for statutory carbon budgets and links supporting analysis and factsheets.
Policy packages and quantified pathways must remain distinct from observed emissions.

sources.title: CBGDP Section 14 Report accessible webpage
facts: Updated 23 June 2026.
The report describes government proposals and policies to enable carbon budgets to be met.
Sector policy contributions and projected savings are not direct emissions measurements.

sources.title: CBGDP technical annex accessible webpage
facts: Updated 23 June 2026.
The annex covers baseline emissions, emissions analysis, sector modelling and wider analysis.
Modelled baseline and pathway outputs require explicit separation from observed inventory data.

sources.title: CBGDP Heat and buildings factsheet
facts: Published 23 June 2026.
The investor factsheet summarises current heat and buildings policies and interventions.
Investment opportunity and policy timing do not provide building or parcel GHG observations.

sources.title: Unlocking the benefits of the clean energy economy accessible webpage
facts: Updated 23 June 2026 as part of the CBGDP package.
It discusses energy security, bills, jobs, health and the natural environment alongside carbon budgets.
Economic and social benefits are not physical emissions measurements.

sources.title: Environmental Improvement Plan Annual Progress Report 2025 to 2026
facts: Published in July 2026 and reports progress through March 2026.
Goal 7 covers climate-change commitments and reports action-status progress.
Completion or progress status of actions is not a measured emissions reduction.

sources.title: Environmental Improvement Plan 2025
facts: The plan identifies climate indicators including greenhouse-gas emissions from natural resources and the carbon footprint.
Its monitoring framework and commitments are policy architecture rather than parcel observations.

sources.title: NAEI Greenhouse Gas Emissions Data
facts: Last updated 9 June 2026.
The page lists the 2026 UK GHG Inventory 1990 to 2024, 2026 source pivot table and 2026 devolved inventories.
Data selectors, pivot tables and maps require scope and geography checks before use.

sources.title: NAEI UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory 1990 to 2024
facts: Report date 30 April 2026.
The National Inventory Document includes annexes and supporting energy, agriculture and forest-stratification data.
National inventory estimates do not imply cadastral parcel attribution.

sources.title: NAEI devolved GHG inventories 1990 to 2024
facts: Report date 9 June 2026.
It provides GHG inventories for England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland for 1990 to 2024.
Country inventories remain aggregate estimates and are not parcel observations.

sources.title: NAEI UK Informative Inventory Report 1990 to 2024
facts: Report date 12 March 2026.
The page records a correction concerning the vintage of road-transport mileage-split data.
Correction and input-vintage provenance must be preserved when reusing inventory methods.

sources.title: NAEI greenhouse-gas reports catalogue
facts: The current catalogue lists the 2026 devolved and UK GHG inventory reports.
A catalogue is provenance/navigation evidence and not an independent emissions measurement.

sources.title: NAEI Data Archive
facts: The archive provides prior versions of GHG pivot tables and other NAEI datasets.
Archived vintages must not silently supersede current inventory data.

sources.title: Final UK greenhouse gas emissions statistics 1990 to 2024
facts: Published 5 February 2026 and updated 25 June 2026.
The accredited statistics provide territorial emissions by source, end-user reallocations and SIC data; all years are revised and supersede prior estimates.
Source, end-user and SIC representations must not be mixed or promoted to parcel observations.

sources.title: National Data Library final UK greenhouse gas emissions
facts: Last updated 25 June 2026.
The catalogue links the 2024 final source, end-user and SIC datasets.
A catalogue mirror is not independent physical evidence and must retain DESNZ provenance.

sources.title: Planned methodology changes for UK GHG emissions
facts: Updated 15 January 2026 with the 2026 methodology note.
Annual methodological improvements can revise the full historical time series.
Method notes are not measured emissions values.

sources.title: UK GHG emissions statistics 2026 planned methodology changes
facts: Updated 15 January 2026.
The note states its method-change impacts were provisional until the February 2026 final statistical release.
Provisional method impacts must not override later final statistics.

sources.title: UK greenhouse gas emissions 2025 final figures announcement
facts: The announcement gives a provisional February 2027 release date.
It is a future release announcement and contains no final 2025 observed dataset as of 26 July 2026.

sources.title: Annual statement of emissions for 2024
facts: Published 23 March 2026 under section 16 of the Climate Change Act 2008.
It sets out calculation of the net UK carbon account for 2024, the second year of the fourth carbon budget.
The statutory carbon account is an accounting construct and must not be conflated with a parcel emission measurement.

sources.title: Annual statement of emissions for 2024 accessible webpage
facts: Published 23 March 2026.
The accessible statement separates UK GHG emissions from calculation of the net UK carbon account.
Carbon-budget accounting and physical territorial emissions require separate semantics.

sources.title: Annual statements of emissions collection
facts: The collection lists annual statements required by section 16 of the Climate Change Act.
It is a statutory-report catalogue, not a new independent emissions observation.

sources.title: CCUS non-pipeline transport consultation
facts: Published 5 February 2026 and updated 23 February 2026; the consultation closed 1 May 2026.
It seeks views on support, fees, risk allocation, regulation and operations for CO2 non-pipeline transport.
Consultation proposals and prospective project data are not verified captured, transported or stored CO2 quantities.

sources.title: CCUS NPT consultation accessible webpage
facts: Updated 23 February 2026.
The page says government aims to respond in 2027 after assessing consultation evidence.
A closed consultation remains policy-development evidence rather than an implemented measurement regime.

sources.title: UK ETS regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines consultation
facts: Published 12 March 2026 and consultation closed 4 June 2026.
It considers streamlining UK ETS permits for CCS pipelines crossing multiple jurisdictions.
Permit structure and regulatory jurisdiction do not quantify captured, leaked or stored CO2.

sources.title: UK ETS cross-boundary CCS pipelines accessible webpage
facts: Issued 12 March 2026.
The accessible consultation discusses options to reduce multiple permit requirements and simplify monitoring and enforcement.
Regulatory simplification is not a physical emissions observation.
